text:
alex: Customer (AcmeFin) reports streaming response that ends up as invalid JSON after client auto-resume. They see a truncated fragment, client reconnects, and the next fragment is a continuation but ends up producing a broken document on the client side.

alex: Example captured from their client (showing chunk boundaries they annotated)
[CHUNK 1]
{"id":"abc123","events":[{"type":"start","actor":"system"}

[CHUNK 2 - after reconnect]
,{"ts":1625244000}],"meta":{"model":"gpt-x"}}

alex: If you naively concatenate the chunks you get: {"id":"abc123","events":[{"type":"start","actor":"system"},{"ts":1625244000}],...} which is invalid because the second piece begins with a leading comma and a lone object instead of a continued array item boundary. Customer's parser fails with "Unexpected token , at position 123".

ingrid: Thanks — can you attach request_id and the raw bytes (hexdump) if available? Also which SDK/version?

alex: request_id=rid_0a1b2c3d. Customer reproduces with their internal proxy that cuts the socket ~4s into the stream. SDK is node-sdk v1.4.2. Repro curl they used:
```
curl -N -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -d '{"prompt":"stream test","stream":true}' \
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate?model=gpt-x
```
They say their proxy does an immediate reconnect and the sdk auto-resumes.

ben: This looks like a "stitching" problem when upstream cut happens at an arbitrary chunk boundary. Two causes to consider: (1) server is sending partial JSON tokens (we expect SSE with complete event payloads), or (2) SDK/agent is trying to merge separate SSE event payloads into a single JSON document. Do we have raw SSE frames from the ingress?

deploy-bot: ingress: upstream connection closed (ECONNRESET) for rid_0a1b2c3d at 2026-03-17T12:34:56Z

ingrid: Pasted the ingress trace from the edge for that request_id:
```
[12:34:51.123] accept connection
[12:34:52.901] forward to worker-7
[12:34:55.987] worker-7: sent event (bytes=438) // last byte = 0x7d ('}')
[12:34:55.988] upstream FIN from client-proxy (unexpected)
[12:34:56.001] edge tried reconnect -> new socket opened -> forwarded to worker-7 with resume_hint=chunkseq:17
[12:34:56.050] worker-7: sent event (bytes=92) // starts with 0x2c (',') then 0x7b ('{')
```

alex: That log is the smoking gun — worker sent a chunk ending with '}' (but likely mid-array) then after reconnect sent a chunk that starts with ',' + '{'. If client reassembly is naive (concatenate stream) it yields a leading comma between top-level tokens. Parser fails.

ben: Short-term mitigation: we can advise customers to set the SDK option `streamAtomic: true` (server will buffer until full JSON object/array boundaries are emitted) — does that option exist for this customer? If not, we should document `X-Redwood-Stream-Mode: atomic` header as a supported workaround. Also encourage keeping proxy idle timeouts > 30s.

ingrid: Can we confirm that `streamAtomic` is safe? We need a customer-facing workaround text to send now. Accounts wants something they can apply without code changes.

ben: Confirming—server-side can gate to emit only complete JSON events when streamAtomic is set; it may add a small latency (~30-120ms) in worst-case. I'll open a short-term server-side flag to force atomic emission for affected customers. Long-term we should add explicit continuation tokens to SSE events so SDKs can reassemble reliably.

alex: I'll tell AcmeFin to add the header as a temporary measure and bump their proxy timeouts. Workaround text draft: "If you see JSON parse errors on stream reconnects, please add header `X-Redwood-Stream-Mode: atomic` (or set SDK option `streamAtomic=true`). This causes the server to ensure emitted SSE payloads align with complete JSON boundaries, avoiding mid-token cutoffs. Alternatively, increase proxy idle/keepalive to ≥ 30s to reduce reconnects."

chris: (acct) Please CC me on the customer reply. I'll include AM support hours.

ben: Follow-up action items: ENG-9876 created to add continuation_token and server/SDK stitching logic. Short-term flag `stream-atomic` enabled for AcmeFin (tenant id acct_987).

alex: Thanks — I'll send customer the workaround and mark this P1 until we have the continuation-token rollout.

ingrid: assigning to ben for fix ETA; I'll draft reply and link to docs. :thumbsup:
